description: pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:644-648: `let results = self.aia.batch_fetch(&uri_refs); for (uri, result) in new_uris.iter().zip(results)`. The AiaFetcher::batch_fetch contract says return Vec is aligned-by-index with input URIs (pkix-aia/src/lib.rs:569-572), but the trait default-impl loops calling fetch (same length), and there is no runtime check that overridden implementations honor this. zip() silently truncates to the shorter of the two iterators. A buggy AiaFetcher implementation that returns one fewer result drops one URI silently — that URI is in tried_uris (so it won't be retried) but its result is never consulted. This is a footgun for future contributors writing custom AiaFetchers. Fix: add `assert_eq!(results.len(), uri_refs.len(), "AiaFetcher::batch_fetch must return one result per URI")` immediately after the call. (Or use debug_assert for release-mode laxness — but in security code, panicking on contract violation is the safer default.)
title: build_with_aia trusts batch_fetch return length without assertion
